hints: Remember the Brønsted-Lowry view, an acid is simply a proton ($H^+$) donor, so look for who gives away $H^+$.
In reaction 1, notice $H_2O$ becomes part of $C_2H_6$, so track where that extra $H$ on the ethyl group came from.
In reaction 2, check which reactant actually contains hydrogen to donate, since a species with no $H$ cannot be a Brønsted-Lowry acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Brønsted-Lowry definition**

Great start, keep it simple. A Brønsted-Lowry acid donates a proton ($H^+$) and a base accepts a proton.

Rule to use:
$$\text{acid} \rightarrow H^+ + \text{conjugate base}$$

**Analyse reaction 1**

Look at what happens to the ethyl groups.

$$(C_2H_5)_2Zn + H_2O \rightarrow ZnO + 2C_2H_6$$
Each $C_2H_5$ fragment gains one $H$ to become $C_2H_6$. That $H^+$ must come from $H_2O$. So $H_2O$ donates protons and acts as the Brønsted-Lowry acid.

**Analyse reaction 2**

Now apply the same hydrogen check.

$$H_2O + ZnO + 2OH^- \rightarrow Zn(OH)_4^{2-}$$
$ZnO$ contains no hydrogen at all, so it cannot donate $H^+$. Therefore it cannot be a Brønsted-Lowry acid. $H_2O$ is the only proton-containing reactant that can donate $H^+$ to form the $OH$ groups in $Zn(OH)_4^{2-}$, so $H_2O$ is again the Brønsted-Lowry acid.

**Conclude the pair**

Both reactions use $H_2O$ as the proton donor. That gives $H_2O$ in reaction 1 and $H_2O$ in reaction 2.

options.A: Incorrect. $(C_2H_5)_2Zn$ does not donate $H^+$, it accepts $H^+$ on its ethyl groups to make $C_2H_6$. The proton donor in reaction 1 is $H_2O$.
options.B: Correct. In reaction 1, $H_2O$ donates $H^+$ to $C_2H_5$ to form $C_2H_6$. In reaction 2, $ZnO$ has no $H$ to donate, so $H_2O$ is again the only possible Brønsted-Lowry acid.
options.C: Incorrect for reaction 2. $ZnO$ contains no hydrogen, so it cannot donate a proton. It acts as a Lewis acid by accepting oxide or hydroxide, not as a Brønsted-Lowry acid.
options.D: Incorrect. Reaction 1 is an acid-base reaction because $H_2O$ donates $H^+$ to form $C_2H_6$. Saying it is not acid/base misses this clear proton transfer, and $ZnO$ still cannot be a Brønsted-Lowry acid in reaction 2.
